message.content: Got it. Two things shape the plan — let me pin them down:
message.reasoning_content:
So I'm mapping out the timeline for the Saut project—17 days until the prototype demo on November 15th, with the final report deadline on December 10th. There are some competing priorities though: an IS midterm coming up on November 5th and an AI final on November 20th. The core work still needed is building the intent parser since speech-to-text with Whisper is already done, plus putting together the demo itself. I'm also waiting on a meeting with Dr. Noura to discuss the intent parser before I can finalize the approach.

Now I'm thinking through the actual plan structure and whether to ask about the intent parser design—rule-based and regex patterns versus using an LLM API. Since Dr. Noura's input is pending and this is a critical decision, I should ask Sami about the approach and how many hours per day he can realistically dedicate to this, given that he's juggling exams. I'll frame it as one question covering both the parser strategy and his availability to avoid too many back-and-forths.

function.name: user_input
function.arguments:
{"question":"The intent parser is the big open piece. Which approach do you want to plan for?

1) Rule-based / patterns (fast, offline, safe for demo)
2) LLM-based intent classification (stronger Arabic understanding, needs API + fallback)
3) Hybrid: rules for the 50 recorded commands + LLM fallback for the rest
4) Still undecided — I'll ask Dr. Noura first (plan should keep it flexible)

Also: roughly how many hours/day can you give Saut between now and 15 Nov, knowing the IS midterm is on 5 Nov?"}
